mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to increased near-term discounting of future earnings.
failure_condition: In a rising FEDFUNDS regime without a subsequent earnings surprise, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs over two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward 60-day return as it signals labor market resilience and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS[t+1] > PAYEMS[t] and PAYEMS[t+2] > PAYEMS[t+1] and (PAYEMS[t+2] - PAYEMS[t]) >= 50000
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, forward returns do not exceed the average of the previous 12 months' 60-day returns during similar labor market conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2% in the following 20-day window, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting optimism about consumer demand.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 50 such positive-demand-shock windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% followed by a rebound to pre-decline levels within 10 days predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals supply-side weakness and possible market correction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO[t+1] < INDPRO[t] and INDPRO[t+2] >= INDPRO[t] and (INDPRO[t+2] - INDPRO[t+1]) / INDPRO[t+1] >= -0.03
regime_hint: Supply contraction followed by quick recovery
failure_condition: During analogous supply contraction-rebound episodes, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced recession fears and lower discounting of equity valuations.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following similar three-month UNRATE declines, forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% over the next month indicates dual demand drivers, which predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return due to stronger economic momentum.
failure_condition: During analogous interaction-driven demand upswings, the 20-day forward return does not outperform the average of prior dual-demand episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI) by at least 1% in a single month followed by a sustained 2% increase over the next 60 days is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals inflationary pressure and potential policy tightening anticipation.
regime_hint: Sudden inflation deceleration followed by reacceleration
failure_condition: In 60-day windows with similar CPI patterns, the forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) lags the 3-month moving average of HOUST (retail sales) by at least 10%, it indicates supply-side lag and predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as the market anticipates slower growth.
regime_hint: Supply lags behind demand over multi-month horizon
failure_condition: During analogous lag episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
